title: Reject link-layer encrypted payloads consistently
description: C currently AES-encrypts E=1 frames and cannot receive its own unsigned encrypted output; Python/Rust reject encrypted frames and the draft treats E as opaque upper-layer encryption. Make all link boundaries reject E=1 until a coordinated encryption design exists, update C tests, and remove contradictory C AES behavior from the active path.
close_reason: E=1 rejection confirmed at every boundary: C frame.c parse/write return -EPROTONOSUPPORT (encryption checked first, beats reserved bit), lichen_link_rx rejects, TX never sets E; Python raises EncryptedFrameError on parse and refuses serialize; Rust returns FrameError::EncryptedUnsupported both ways. Removed contradictory AES remnants from C link layer: deleted unreferenced link_nonce.h, dropped select LICHEN_CRYPTO_AES_CCM from LICHEN_LINK Kconfig, corrected stale AES-CCM MIC prose in Kconfig/CMakeLists/link_ctx.c comments. Verified: frame_test 16/16, clang -fsyntax-only clean, pytest -k 'link or frame' 1111 passed/13 skipped (project venv), cargo test -p lichen-link all ok, clippy --all-features -D warnings clean.
